programme.title: Peter Rabbit
programme.desc: Peter proves he's got what it takes to be part of the squirrel tribe when he competes for his own treetop hideout.

programme.title: Octonauts
programme.desc: Animated deep sea adventure series. Captain Barnacles and his intrepid band of explorers roam the oceans in search of adventure and fun. Whether it's a perilous voyage to the bottom of the sea or the piratey pursuit of a giant squid, the Octonauts leap into action and always prove that eight heads are better than one. When important objects go missing from their ship, the Octonauts stake out the thief, who turns out to be a decorator crab, stealing their things to decorate his shell.

programme.title: Numberblocks
programme.desc: Welcome to the fabulous, fun fruit factory, where Three's super fruit-sorting machines aren't giving her any fruit. Find out how to split numbers into smaller numbers with the Numberblocks.

programme.title: Alphablocks
programme.desc: CH and SH go head to head in the Alphablocks Games and pit a ship and a shop against a chip and a chop. This episode has fun with the '-ch-' and '-sh-' digraphs and the words shop, chop, chip, ship, shin, chin, shed, mash, cash and sash.

programme.title: Nick Cope's Popcast
programme.desc: After a successful trip to the dentist, Nick tells Norman all about the tooth fairy. Does the tooth fairy visit dogs? Along with the help of the Popcasters, they write a song about looking after your teeth.

programme.title: Playtime Towers
programme.desc: Bella and Lift play counting games with their favourite red bouncy ball. When Bella slams the ball really high, it travels all the way to the Ice Disco, giving Hettie the Yeti an idea for a bounce dance! In Boxtropolis, Sketch makes splats of paint to create a picture of three bouncy balls that look like a kangaroo! In the Fortress of Fun, Kingsley and Queenie can’t decide which ball to play with, so they ask the Playtimers for help by playing ‘Bally Ball Snap’.

programme.title: Bing
programme.desc: Bing and Pando experiment with Bing's toy train on the Fun Fort in the playground. The train is good at going over bridges and brilliant at going down the slide. But when Bing slides it off the roof of the playhouse, the train crashes and breaks. Bing is upset until he realises that the pieces fit together to make something completely different.

programme.title: Yakka Dee!
programme.desc: Dee encourages a friend to say ‘elf’, and we go on a whirlwind word adventure. Today, we meet lots of little elves. We see pointy ears and hats and stripy tights. We meet elves who are ice skating, one sitting on a shelf and another who is really cheeky! The journey is repeated with some special surprises along the way, and everyone has a boogie when Dee’s friend finally succeeds in saying today’s word.

programme.title: Lu & the Bally Bunch
programme.desc: Lu finds a special leaf for the autumn collage.

programme.title: Piggy Builders
programme.desc: Fred and Dana ask the Piggies to plan fun outdoor games for Keith and Rebecca. Each piggy comes up with an idea, but Cesar’s is so ambitious that he can’t tackle it alone!

programme.title: Twirlywoos
programme.desc: The Twirlywoos are in a park, where they watch a man walking along a path. They see him step over a puddle, and start to follow him. Each time the man reaches a puddle he steps over it, and the Twirlywoos copy him and jump over themselves. In the end they reach a huge puddle which is too big for them to get over and they land with a splash! As the Hooter calls them home, they fly over the man and drip water on him. He mistakes this for rain and puts up his umbrella. Peekaboo has some spongy bricks which assemble themselves into a wall. The Twirlywoos return to the boat, and Peekaboo hides from them behind the wall. Unfortunately he makes a noise which the Twirlywoos hear, and as they go around the wall he has to jump over it to avoid being seen by them. They hear him and go back around the wall to investigate, so Peekaboo has to jump over it again. Eventually the Twirlywoos decide to go over the wall instead of around it and Great BigHoo causes the wall to fall into a heap of bricks. The Twirlywoos chase after their rings and the coast is clear for Peekaboo to take his bricks back to his house.

programme.title: Something Special
programme.desc: Justin and his friends host a summer party and pick vegetables to make a delicious salad. Mr Tumble’s also hosting a party, but he struggles to find a garden game that he’s good at.

programme.title: Teletubbies
programme.desc: The Teletubbies take it in turns to go up and down on the Dup Dup. Sometimes they go fast and sometimes they go slow - and even the Noo-noo has a go!

programme.title: The Baby Club
programme.desc: Giovanna and Baby Bear welcome babies DJ, Holly, Li-Li, Luke, George, Otis and their grown-ups to The Baby Club. Inside everyone’s bags in this episode are Bowls which are explored through discovery, play, song and story. Grown-ups at home are encouraged to take part by hiding baby appropriate bowls inside a fabric bag or pillowcase for them to reveal and explore with their baby! The fun rhyme ‘Pat-a-cake’ features, as does a story involving Baby Bear. Plus, the Action Song gets everyone moving about, before some calm time with bubbles and the Goodbye Song.

programme.title: Tiny Tunes
programme.desc: In Tall Trees Forest, Lisa and the children have bubbly fun washing toy clothes, learning British Sign Language signs for jungle, clothes and washing, then they sing and sign Down in the Jungle.

programme.title: I Can Grow It
programme.desc: Aaron is joined by Jackson and Mia as they discover how to feed the garden, and the special role wiggly worms have in making sure the plants stay happy and healthy.

programme.title: Monster Makes
programme.desc: Rebecca and Murphi are playing hide-and-seek. Murphi is so difficult to find that he comes out of hiding to help Rebecca make a cardboard tube tracker dog. The Mini Monsters make paper bag monsters, and Rebecca’s Grandpa calls to share his fishing frustrations. The Recycling Express brings a shoebox, inspiring a mega monster idea - a magnificent monster! And the Tiny Helpers are on hand to help make the hutch.

programme.title: Vegesaurs
programme.desc: Ginger teaches the baby Pea-Rexes a new survival skill through a game of hide-and-seek.

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: At the weekend, Bluey and Bingo are playing in the garden with Dad. Bingo gets upset when she discovers a walking leaf insect, but Dad is too caught up in the game to notice.

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: The Squirrels have just got some new walkie-talkies and are having so much fun with them. Duggee calls the Squirrels to come for some blueberry juice, but as Tag is running, he trips over a car and falls through a secret door in the wall! Communicating through his walkie-talkie, Tag doesn’t know where he is. He can see lots and lots of things around him but no one has any idea where this room is in the house!

programme.title: Let's Go for a Walk
programme.desc: Ranger Hamza and the Ramblers walk through a forest to the beach in order to draw pictures in the sand. On the way, they find a big rock, copy a pigeon having a drink, make patterns in the water and even spot a tree that looks like a spider!

programme.title: Our Family
programme.desc: Ted and his family head to the beach, and Ted tries his hand at making a sandcastle. When it doesn’t go quite to plan, Dad shows him some top tips. After some fun flying a kite, the family enjoy a game of catch. And what trip to the beach is complete without an ice cream?

programme.title: My World Kitchen
programme.desc: Izaac is making a traditional recipe from his home county of Lancashire. The Chorley cakes are made from circles of pastry filled with a fruity filling of dried cherries and currants. Izaac works hard tickling the flour and butter together before turning it into dough, which he then has to carefully roll out. When Izaac's friends arrive he gives them a red rose, the symbol of Lancashire. Will Izaac's friends guess the special ingredient and will they enjoy it in his Chorley cakes?

programme.title: Maddie's Do You Know?
programme.desc: In today's episode, Maddie is outdoors finding out about things that use the wind. She finds out how a kite works when it flies high in the sky, shows us how to measure the wind speed, and uses a slow-motion camera to explain how a kite catches the wind to stay in the air. Next, Maddie finds out how electricity is made on a wind farm. She visits a wind turbine to see how it turns wind energy into electricity.

programme.title: Dog Squad
programme.desc: Tinks is a disability assistance dog for her owner Charli, who has a condition that makes it painful for her to pick things up or to push and pull things. Tinks uses her super fetch skills to help Charli every day. The smallest of the Dog Squad gang, Tinks is a little Lhasa apso with lots of big dog energy. Charli is meeting her friend Annabel for lunch at the local café. They haven’t been out for a lunch treat for ages, and the café’s speciality is Tinks’s favourite – chicken. First, Charli parks her car using her blue parking badge and then gets her wheelchair out of the boot using a hoist. Tinks then helps Charli go into the café, find a table and go to the counter to order their lunch. But when the café owner sees Tinks, he tells Charli that they only allow in guide dogs and that Tinks will have to wait outside. Brave Tinks summons all her big dog energy to help Charli persuade the owner to let them stay and enjoy their chicken sandwich.

programme.title: Go Wild
programme.desc: Aneeshwar and Lizzie meet two gentle giants. Priscilla is a 30-year-old Galapagos tortoise, who loves to be fed lettuce and to have her neck scratched. Next, Aneeshwar and Lizzie meet a giant African land snail. These snails can weigh up to 1kg - that's almost the weight of a pineapple. Aneeshwar and Lizzie place the giant snail on a glass frame, so they can look underneath the snail to see how it uses its long foot and a helping of gloopy slime to move. Finally, Aneeshwar and Lizzie discover what the wild connection is between these two incredible animals.

programme.title: Waffle the Wonder Dog
programme.desc: Connie and Ruby move into Maple Close with their dog, Jelly. Mrs Hobbs can't help but express her disapproval. She hates dogs and now there'll be another one living in close proximity. Waffle is not allowed to go on a family camping trip but accidentally goes on a different adventure!

programme.title: Puffin Rock
programme.desc: When Baba takes Bernie’s best shell, Oona helps him make amends.

programme.title: Small Potatoes
programme.desc: Animated series about a group of singing potatoes. Potatoes from around the world celebrate the similarities and differences we all share.

programme.title: Yukee
programme.desc: A famous soul singer is coming to perform in the garden, but no one knows what they look like. Meanwhile, a cheeky little mouse with a great big voice has appeared in the Sunhouse.

programme.title: Maddie + Triggs
programme.desc: Maddie and Triggs are helping Mum babysit their little neighbour Sally. She's a toddler and is just learning to speak. Maddie really wants Sally to enjoy herself, but no matter what she offers, Sally just keeps saying 'no'! Could it be that this trickster toddler is saying 'no' even when she means something else?

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: The Squirrels go out for a walk but can't find a way back to the clubhouse. Through a series of unusual methods, the Squirrels learn all about direction and how to find their way to the clubhouse.

programme.title: Numberblocks
programme.desc: One discovers it's tricky to play tennis when you're the only block in the world. She bumps into a magic mirror and meets another One, and they join forces to make Two. Learn a thing or two about adding with the Numberblocks.

programme.title: Alphablocks
programme.desc: Alphablock S loves to look at the night sky with her friends. She is delighted when a STAR appears and invites them to follow it. They make a BROOM to sit on, but it is not big enough. So, they make two BROOMS. The Alphablocks take off, and the star leads them on an exciting ride. Passing through a STORM is a bit too exciting, so they decide to make the sky BRIGHT. It transforms, and the star takes them on a magical journey through the Northern Lights.

programme.title: Something Special
programme.desc: Justin and his friends go up, up, up and away having fun playing aeroplanes. Meanwhile, Mr Tumble turns his home into a hotel and has some very important guests flying in.

programme.title: Teletubbies
programme.desc: The Teletubbies go 'this way, that way' on a Tubby Car journey to the Hidey Hup. The Tubby Spinny goes 'this way, that way' too.

programme.title: Ranger Hamza's Eco Quest
programme.desc: Ranger Hamza and the Ramblers discover how sand dunes play an important role in the environment. They find out how sand dunes are made and that they can be great places for lots of plants to grow and creatures to live. They also learn that they can change over time and help prevent erosion from the wind and sea. On the way they spot a beautiful moth and play a game all about the food chain.

programme.title: Football Fantastics
programme.desc: Sophie must infiltrate the sports hall without disturbing a relaxation class Val is running. Her aim is to retrieve bibs, goals and a big bag of footballs.

programme.title: Grace's Amazing Machines
programme.desc: CBeebies’ very own motorbike rider Grace shows off three amazing machines that help make roads! Grace helps operate a road planer, checks out a road-printing machine and then has a go in a road paver!

programme.desc: It's class photo day, but no-one can work out why Biscuit has arrived with a box on her head. When the pups realise she is embarrassed about her 'fur' style, they work together to make her feel better by making paper hats for everyone to wear. Biscuit finally understands the importance of just being herself.

programme.title: The Neighbourhood
programme.desc: Graham Norton hosts The Neighbourhood, a brand-new high stakes, street-sized popularity contest. Two households come under fire at the third removal, and another realises they must go against their friendships and vote tactically to make it further in the competition. Following the tense removal, Graham hosts a cocktail party for the neighbours to relax. Unbeknownst to them, this event serves to secretly introduce a new family, allowing them to spy on the existing residents before their official introduction. This is the final arrival, as the Neighbourhood gates are now closed and neighbours will only be leaving from now on. Graham makes a night-time visit to bestow the title of 'The Secret Power House' upon one lucky household via a game of chance. The winners are granted the power to sway the course of the game and favour their own house. However, all of their choices will be disclosed at the end of the week, raising the question: how will they choose to wield this newfound power?

programme.title: The Assembly
programme.desc: Nicola Sturgeon faces the grilling of a lifetime from a cast of autistic and learning-disabled interviewers. Why did she separate from her husband? Who does she like least in politics? From her arrest to her love life, nothing is off limits as The Assembly get straight to the heart of a former leader - now unleashed. As the questions come thick and fast, Sturgeon opens up about grief, guilt and the loss of her baby, reflects on her complicated relationship with her former mentor Alex Salmond, and reveals what she'd say to her younger self. Along the way, there's talk of wine, Buckfast, Sean Connery, and whether she's due a new hairstyle. From the deeply personal to the downright cheeky, this is Nicola Sturgeon as you've never seen her before. Expect honesty, emotion, laughter - and a few moments that take everyone by surprise.

However, in the upcoming 'Neighbourhood Watch' immunity challenge, the question looms: will they prioritise their own gain or help out their neighbours? Who will they choose and will this decision come back to haunt them when Graham later reveals who the Power House is? Strategy takes centre stage as one household secures vital immunity.

However, in the upcoming 'Neighbourhood Watch' immunity challenge, the question looms: will they prioritise their own gain or help out their neighbours? Who will they choose and will this decision come back to haunt them when Graham later reveals who the Power House is? Strategy takes centre stage as one household secures vital immunity.

programme.title: The Neighbourhood
programme.desc: Graham Norton hosts The Neighbourhood, a brand-new high stakes, street-sized popularity contest. Two households come under fire at the third removal, and another realises they must go against their friendships and vote tactically to make it further in the competition. Following the tense removal, Graham hosts a cocktail party for the neighbours to relax. Unbeknownst to them, this event serves to secretly introduce a new family, allowing them to spy on the existing residents before their official introduction. This is the final arrival, as the Neighbourhood gates are now closed and neighbours will only be leaving from now on. Graham makes a night-time visit to bestow the title of 'The Secret Power House' upon one lucky household via a game of chance. The winners are granted the power to sway the course of the game and favour their own house. However, all of their choices will be disclosed at the end of the week, raising the question: how will they choose to wield this newfound power?

programme.title: The Assembly
programme.desc: Nicola Sturgeon faces the grilling of a lifetime from a cast of autistic and learning-disabled interviewers. Why did she separate from her husband? Who does she like least in politics? From her arrest to her love life, nothing is off limits as The Assembly get straight to the heart of a former leader - now unleashed. As the questions come thick and fast, Sturgeon opens up about grief, guilt and the loss of her baby, reflects on her complicated relationship with her former mentor Alex Salmond, and reveals what she'd say to her younger self. Along the way, there's talk of wine, Buckfast, Sean Connery, and whether she's due a new hairstyle. From the deeply personal to the downright cheeky, this is Nicola Sturgeon as you've never seen her before. Expect honesty, emotion, laughter - and a few moments that take everyone by surprise.

programme.title: The Neighbourhood
programme.desc: The secret Power House wastes no time to curry favour with a neighbour by gifting a lavish hamper. However, in the upcoming 'Neighbourhood Watch' immunity challenge, the question looms: will they prioritise their own gain or help out their neighbours? Strange things have been occurring on the close after dark, and for the next challenge the households will be on Neighbourhood Watch duty! Two members of each household, secretly chosen by the Power House, must stay up late observing all the Neighbourhood happenings. They must write what they see in their notebooks, and the following day Graham hosts The Neighbourhood Watch Quiz where their knowledge and attention to detail is tested - but there is a sting in the tale as the Power House also gets to disadvantage one household and take away their notebook! Who will they choose and will this decision come back to haunt them when Graham later reveals who the Power House is? Strategy takes centre stage as one household secures vital immunity.

programme.title: The Neighbourhood
programme.desc: Graham Norton hosts The Neighbourhood, a brand-new high stakes, street-sized popularity contest. Two households come under fire at the third removal, and another realises they must go against their friendships and vote tactically to make it further in the competition. Following the tense removal, Graham hosts a cocktail party for the neighbours to relax. Unbeknownst to them, this event serves to secretly introduce a new family, allowing them to spy on the existing residents before their official introduction. This is the final arrival, as the Neighbourhood gates are now closed and neighbours will only be leaving from now on. Graham makes a night-time visit to bestow the title of 'The Secret Power House' upon one lucky household via a game of chance. The winners are granted the power to sway the course of the game and favour their own house. However, all of their choices will be disclosed at the end of the week, raising the question: how will they choose to wield this newfound power?

programme.title: The Assembly
programme.desc: Nicola Sturgeon faces the grilling of a lifetime from a cast of autistic and learning-disabled interviewers. Why did she separate from her husband? Who does she like least in politics? From her arrest to her love life, nothing is off limits as The Assembly get straight to the heart of a former leader - now unleashed. As the questions come thick and fast, Sturgeon opens up about grief, guilt and the loss of her baby, reflects on her complicated relationship with her former mentor Alex Salmond, and reveals what she'd say to her younger self. Along the way, there's talk of wine, Buckfast, Sean Connery, and whether she's due a new hairstyle. From the deeply personal to the downright cheeky, this is Nicola Sturgeon as you've never seen her before. Expect honesty, emotion, laughter - and a few moments that take everyone by surprise.

programme.title: The Neighbourhood
programme.desc: The secret Power House wastes no time to curry favour with a neighbour by gifting a lavish hamper. However, in the upcoming 'Neighbourhood Watch' immunity challenge, the question looms: will they prioritise their own gain or help out their neighbours? Strange things have been occurring on the close after dark, and for the next challenge the households will be on Neighbourhood Watch duty! Two members of each household, secretly chosen by the Power House, must stay up late observing all the Neighbourhood happenings. They must write what they see in their notebooks, and the following day Graham hosts The Neighbourhood Watch Quiz where their knowledge and attention to detail is tested - but there is a sting in the tale as the Power House also gets to disadvantage one household and take away their notebook! Who will they choose and will this decision come back to haunt them when Graham later reveals who the Power House is? Strategy takes centre stage as one household secures vital immunity.

programme.title: The Dark Knight
programme.desc: Oscar-winning action crime drama sequel. A criminal madman known as the Joker starts wreaking havoc on the people of Gotham by murdering innocent civilians in an attempt to force the vigilante Batman into revealing his true identity - meanwhile, new district attorney Harvey Dent announces his plan to eradicate the Mob. Bruce Wayne - also known as the Caped Crusader - must now face one of the greatest psychological tests of his ability to fight injustice in order to come out on top once more...

programme.title: The Neighbourhood
programme.desc: Graham Norton hosts The Neighbourhood, a brand-new high stakes, street-sized popularity contest. Two households come under fire at the third removal, and another realises they must go against their friendships and vote tactically to make it further in the competition. Following the tense removal, Graham hosts a cocktail party for the neighbours to relax. Unbeknownst to them, this event serves to secretly introduce a new family, allowing them to spy on the existing residents before their official introduction. This is the final arrival, as the Neighbourhood gates are now closed and neighbours will only be leaving from now on. Graham makes a night-time visit to bestow the title of 'The Secret Power House' upon one lucky household via a game of chance. The winners are granted the power to sway the course of the game and favour their own house. However, all of their choices will be disclosed at the end of the week, raising the question: how will they choose to wield this newfound power?

programme.title: The Assembly
programme.desc: Nicola Sturgeon faces the grilling of a lifetime from a cast of autistic and learning-disabled interviewers. Why did she separate from her husband? Who does she like least in politics? From her arrest to her love life, nothing is off limits as The Assembly get straight to the heart of a former leader - now unleashed. As the questions come thick and fast, Sturgeon opens up about grief, guilt and the loss of her baby, reflects on her complicated relationship with her former mentor Alex Salmond, and reveals what she'd say to her younger self. Along the way, there's talk of wine, Buckfast, Sean Connery, and whether she's due a new hairstyle. From the deeply personal to the downright cheeky, this is Nicola Sturgeon as you've never seen her before. Expect honesty, emotion, laughter - and a few moments that take everyone by surprise.

programme.title: The Neighbourhood
programme.desc: Graham Norton hosts The Neighbourhood, a brand-new high stakes, street-sized popularity contest. Two households come under fire at the third removal, and another realises they must go against their friendships and vote tactically to make it further in the competition. Following the tense removal, Graham hosts a cocktail party for the neighbours to relax. Unbeknownst to them, this event serves to secretly introduce a new family, allowing them to spy on the existing residents before their official introduction. This is the final arrival, as the Neighbourhood gates are now closed and neighbours will only be leaving from now on. Graham makes a night-time visit to bestow the title of 'The Secret Power House' upon one lucky household via a game of chance. The winners are granted the power to sway the course of the game and favour their own house. However, all of their choices will be disclosed at the end of the week, raising the question: how will they choose to wield this newfound power?

programme.title: The Assembly
programme.desc: Nicola Sturgeon faces the grilling of a lifetime from a cast of autistic and learning-disabled interviewers. Why did she separate from her husband? Who does she like least in politics? From her arrest to her love life, nothing is off limits as The Assembly get straight to the heart of a former leader - now unleashed. As the questions come thick and fast, Sturgeon opens up about grief, guilt and the loss of her baby, reflects on her complicated relationship with her former mentor Alex Salmond, and reveals what she'd say to her younger self. Along the way, there's talk of wine, Buckfast, Sean Connery, and whether she's due a new hairstyle. From the deeply personal to the downright cheeky, this is Nicola Sturgeon as you've never seen her before. Expect honesty, emotion, laughter - and a few moments that take everyone by surprise.

programme.title: The Neighbourhood
programme.desc: Graham Norton hosts The Neighbourhood, a brand-new high stakes, street-sized popularity contest. Two households come under fire at the third removal, and another realises they must go against their friendships and vote tactically to make it further in the competition. Following the tense removal, Graham hosts a cocktail party for the neighbours to relax. Unbeknownst to them, this event serves to secretly introduce a new family, allowing them to spy on the existing residents before their official introduction. This is the final arrival, as the Neighbourhood gates are now closed and neighbours will only be leaving from now on. Graham makes a night-time visit to bestow the title of 'The Secret Power House' upon one lucky household via a game of chance. The winners are granted the power to sway the course of the game and favour their own house. However, all of their choices will be disclosed at the end of the week, raising the question: how will they choose to wield this newfound power?

programme.title: The Assembly
programme.desc: Nicola Sturgeon faces the grilling of a lifetime from a cast of autistic and learning-disabled interviewers. Why did she separate from her husband? Who does she like least in politics? From her arrest to her love life, nothing is off limits as The Assembly get straight to the heart of a former leader - now unleashed. As the questions come thick and fast, Sturgeon opens up about grief, guilt and the loss of her baby, reflects on her complicated relationship with her former mentor Alex Salmond, and reveals what she'd say to her younger self. Along the way, there's talk of wine, Buckfast, Sean Connery, and whether she's due a new hairstyle. From the deeply personal to the downright cheeky, this is Nicola Sturgeon as you've never seen her before. Expect honesty, emotion, laughter - and a few moments that take everyone by surprise.

programme.desc: The secret Power House wastes no time to curry favour with a neighbour by gifting a lavish hamper. However, in the upcoming 'Neighbourhood Watch' immunity challenge, the question looms: will they prioritise their own gain or help out their neighbours? Strange things have been occurring on the close after dark, and for the next challenge the households will be on Neighbourhood Watch duty! programme.title: The Neighbourhood
programme.desc: Graham Norton hosts The Neighbourhood, a brand-new high stakes, street-sized popularity contest. Two households come under fire at the third removal, and another realises they must go against their friendships and vote tactically to make it further in the competition. Following the tense removal, Graham hosts a cocktail party for the neighbours to relax. Unbeknownst to them, this event serves to secretly introduce a new family, allowing them to spy on the existing residents before their official introduction. This is the final arrival, as the Neighbourhood gates are now closed and neighbours will only be leaving from now on. Graham makes a night-time visit to bestow the title of 'The Secret Power House' upon one lucky household via a game of chance. The winners are granted the power to sway the course of the game and favour their own house. However, all of their choices will be disclosed at the end of the week, raising the question: how will they choose to wield this newfound power?

programme.title: The Assembly
programme.desc: Nicola Sturgeon faces the grilling of a lifetime from a cast of autistic and learning-disabled interviewers. Why did she separate from her husband? Who does she like least in politics? From her arrest to her love life, nothing is off limits as The Assembly get straight to the heart of a former leader - now unleashed. As the questions come thick and fast, Sturgeon opens up about grief, guilt and the loss of her baby, reflects on her complicated relationship with her former mentor Alex Salmond, and reveals what she'd say to her younger self. Along the way, there's talk of wine, Buckfast, Sean Connery, and whether she's due a new hairstyle. From the deeply personal to the downright cheeky, this is Nicola Sturgeon as you've never seen her before. Expect honesty, emotion, laughter - and a few moments that take everyone by surprise.
